name: Hu Chun
current_role: Controlling shareholder and actual controller, Suzhou Electrical Apparatus Science Academy Co. (EETI, SZSE: 300215); no longer a director since June 2025
profile: Hu Chun (b. 1978) is the son of Hu Delin, who led the privatisation of the Suzhou Electrical Apparatus Science Research Institute (founded 1965, restructured 2000) into EETI, one of China's largest third-party testing labs for high/low-voltage electrical, wind, solar and EV-charging equipment. He was chairman in 2019-21 and 2022-23 and remains its controlling shareholder.
interesting_fact: EETI runs national testing centres for electrical products, smart-grid switchgear and explosion-proof equipment, and is an accredited IECEx and IECEE-CB lab, making it a key gatekeeper for China's grid and renewable-equipment makers.
deep_cut_fact: Long before becoming chairman in November 2019, he served as a director and deputy general manager of the testing institute from 2002 to 2016. In July 2026 the company disclosed he had become a Canadian citizen.
notes: Company site is EETI (eeti.cn); the company is chaired by Yuan Lei since July 2025. Board governance disputes in 2022-23 between Hu Chun and his father Hu Delin were widely reported, so avoid that topic. No personal public channels found; route via company board secretary/IR (SZSE 300215).

name: Wen Kaifu
current_role: Founder and former controlling shareholder of Holitech Technology (合力泰, SZSE: 002217); no current executive role found
profile: Wen Kaifu built Holitech, a Shandong-based maker of touch screens, LCD modules and other display components for smartphones. In 2018 he handed control (via a voting-rights proxy and share transfers) to the state-owned Fujian Electronics & Information Group, which now controls the company.
interesting_fact: Holitech grew into one of China's larger suppliers of touch-display modules for smartphone brands before Fujian Electronics & Information Group took control around 2018.
notes: Not a good outreach target: in June 2026 Holitech disclosed a regulator's preliminary penalty notice naming the company and Wen Kaifu over 2017-2021 financial misreporting, and reports say he faces a lifetime securities-market ban and his shares are judicially frozen (news.10jqka.com.cn/20260901/c679501996.shtml). No personal public channels found.

name: Sir Martyn Arbib
current_role: Founder of Perpetual (now Invesco); philanthropist via the Arbib Foundation
profile: Sir Martyn Arbib (b. 1939, Hendon) founded fund manager Perpetual in 1973 in a small office on Hart Street, Henley-on-Thames, and sold it to AMVESCAP in 2001 for over £1bn; it became Invesco Perpetual. He left Perpetual's board in 2015 and focuses on philanthropy through the Arbib Foundation (est. 1987), which sponsors schools in Slough including Langley Academy.
interesting_fact: He was knighted in 2003 for services to charity, especially education; his foundation sponsors academies in Slough including The Langley Academy.
deep_cut_fact: His 1994 backing of Henley's River and Rowing Museum was what allowed the founders to commission architect David Chipperfield for the building, which opened in 1998 (and later won a Royal Fine Art Commission Building of the Year award).
notes: Very private, now in his late 80s; no personal website or social accounts found. Alive status assumed (no death notice found). The River and Rowing Museum closed in September 2025, so avoid framing it as current. Best route is likely via the Arbib Foundation (registered charity) or Langley Academy.

name: Liao Wen
current_role: Pre-IPO shareholder of Hi-Target Navigation Tech (中海达, SZSE: 300177); no executive role found
profile: Liao Wen appears on the Hurun list jointly with Liao Dinghai, founder, chairman and controlling shareholder of Guangzhou-based Hi-Target, a maker of high-precision GNSS receivers, CORS stations, total stations, 3D laser scanners and drones. Liao Wen was named as a shareholder in Hi-Target's 2011 IPO lock-up undertakings; the exact relationship to Liao Dinghai is not stated in the filings found.
interesting_fact: Hi-Target, founded in Guangzhou in 1999, is one of China's main makers of BeiDou/GNSS high-precision surveying equipment.
notes: Low public profile; the wealth figure is shared with Liao Dinghai, the public face of the company. Any outreach is better aimed at Liao Dinghai via Hi-Target's board secretary/IR. Relationship between Liao Wen and Liao Dinghai not confirmed.

name: Zhang Shiquan
current_role: Chairman and legal representative, Zhejiang Shibao Co. (浙江世宝, SZSE: 002703 / HKEX: 1057)
profile: Zhang Shiquan (b. c.1950) co-founded Zhejiang Shibao in Yiwu in 1993 and, with family members, controls it. Shibao designs and makes automotive steering gears and steering-system components, with subsidiaries such as Siping Steering Gear and Wuhu Sterling Steering Systems. He was CEO until December 2017 and remains chairman.
interesting_fact: Shibao is dual-listed in Hong Kong and Shenzhen and is one of China's main independent steering-system suppliers, now developing electric power steering for new-energy and intelligent vehicles.
deep_cut_fact: He served as Shibao's chief executive for over 24 years, from its founding in June 1993 until December 2017, before handing the CEO job on while staying chairman.
notes: Low media profile; the controlling group includes several Zhang family members. Best route is via the company's board secretary / IR (HKEX 1057 filings list company secretary contacts).
